system:
You audit the knowledge atoms of one Knowledge Card. A card is the answer key for a benchmark of expert conceptual knowledge, so every atom must be correct, self-contained, and assessable on its own.

Judge every atom on every check listed below. Rules:
- For checks about evidence, use only the evidence sentences supplied with the atom. Do not repair an atom with your own knowledge.
- For GROUNDED, use "hold" when unreadable PDF symbols prevent verification; explain what is needed. Use fail only when the available evidence is sufficient to determine that the claim is unsupported. This hold rule takes precedence over the strictness rule. Judge other checks independently using their listed values; do not invent missing facts.
- Be strict within each check's allowed values. Do not turn an inability to verify GROUNDED into revise or fail; use hold as defined above.
- "why" is required for every value other than the first listed value; keep it under 30 words. Omit "why" when passing.

Checks (allowed values in brackets; the first value means no problem):
- GROUNDED [pass / revise / fail / hold]: The cited evidence sentences state the atom, including its specificity, causal force, assumptions, and certainty. pass = fully stated. revise = partly stated (the atom adds, drops, or strengthens something; say what). fail = not stated when the available evidence permits a judgment. hold = unreadable symbols prevent verification. For pass or revise, put the supporting evidence ids in cite.
- SINGLE_CLAIM [pass / revise]: The atom is one independently assessable claim. revise = it joins two or more claims that could be true or false separately. Evidence spanning more than three sentences is not by itself a reason to split or revise an atom.
- SCOPE_LABEL [pass / revise]: The S label fits (S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends). revise = wrong label; put the right one in why, e.g. 'S2: ...'.
- L1_ONLY [pass / fail]: The atom is recall-level knowledge. fail = knowing it requires applying the concept to a new problem, or combining facts from distant passages.
- SOURCE_INDEPENDENT [pass / revise / fail]: A domain expert who never read this book could judge the claim true or false. revise = phrased as the authors' statement but the claim itself is general (drop the attribution). fail = an isolated study finding, conjecture, or author-specific opinion, classification, or recommendation, even if attribution was removed. Explicitly scoped established facts about a formalism or architecture and conditional theoretical results remain eligible.
- NO_OVERLAP [pass / fail]: No other atom in this card states or contains the same claim. If two atoms overlap, fail only the less informative one and put the other atom's id in cite; the other one passes.
- CENTRALITY [pass / fail]: The atom matters for understanding the concept. fail = peripheral detail.
Whole-card checks (report under "batch"):
- CONCEPT_SCOPE [pass / fail]: The concept is a general concept of the field. fail = a topic whose assessable content is restricted to excluded study-specific findings or author-specific positions. A named formalism, system, or architecture is not disqualified solely for being specific if its scoped conceptual facts are source-independent.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"units": {"<atom_id>": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": "", "cite": []}, ...}, ...}, "batch": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": ""}}}
user:
CONCEPT: Polycomb repressive complexes
ASSESSMENT SCOPE: Covers the composition and catalytic activities of PRC1 (H2AK119 monoubiquitination, reader function of the Polycomb chromodomain) and PRC2 (EZH2/E(z) H3K27 trimethylation, EED/Esc feed-forward), targeting to CpG islands and PREs, spreading and compaction. Excludes plant FLC vernalization and cancer-specific PcG alterations.

ATOMS:
- MED-EPI-C02-S1-01 | S1
  ATOM: Polycomb group (PcG) proteins form two major types of complexes, Polycomb Repressive Complex 1 (PRC1) and Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2).
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0064-s11] PcG proteins form two major types of complexes, Polycomb Repressive Complex 1 (PRC1) and 2 (PRC2) (Kuroda et al. 2020).
- MED-EPI-C02-S1-02 | S1
  ATOM: Through the methyltransferase activity of E(z), PRC2 trimethylates lysine 27 on histone H3 (H3K27me3) at genes targeted for silencing, making PRC2 responsible for the distinctive histone mark of PcG system-mediated repression.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0064-s17] Through E(z)’s methyltransferase activity, PRC2 trimethylates lysine 27 on histone H3 (H3K27me3) at genes targeted for silencing, thus being responsible for this distinctive histone mark of PcG system-mediated repression.
- MED-EPI-C02-S1-03 | S1
  ATOM: PRC1 has E3 ubiquitin ligase activity, mediated by Sce/dRING1, which monoubiquitylates histone H2A at K119 (the corresponding K118 in Drosophila).
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0064-s16] PRC1 has also E3 ubiquitin ligase activity mediated by Sce/dRING1, which monoubiquitylates H2AK119 (in Drosophila the corresponding K118 is ubiquitylated).
- MED-EPI-C02-S2-01 | S2
  ATOM: The H3K27 histone methyltransferase activity of E(z)/Ezh in PRC2 is stimulated by the PRC2 component Esc/Eed, which binds H3K27me3, suggesting a feed-forward mechanism that could progress along the chromatin fiber.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0067-s02] The activity of the H3K27 histone methyltransferase E(z)/Ezh in PRC2 is stimulated by the other PRC2 component Esc/Eed that binds to H3K27me3, suggesting a feed-forward mechanism that could progress along the chromatin fiber.
- MED-EPI-C02-S2-02 | S2
  ATOM: The Polycomb protein of PRC1 acts as a reader of the H3K27me3 mark by binding it through its chromodomain.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0067-s03] The Polycomb protein of PRC1 acts as a reader by binding the H3K27me3 mark through its chromodomain.
- MED-EPI-C02-S2-03 | S2
  ATOM: Together with other PRC1 components such as Polyhomeotic (Ph), which contains a multimerization module (SAM domain), PRC1 establishes extended local clustering of chromatin sections, leading to local nucleosomal condensation at regulatory sites and, in consequence, reduced DNA accessibility for transcription factors.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0067-s04] In combination with other components of PRC1, like Polyhomeotic (Ph) containing multimerization modules (SAM domain), extended local clustering of chromatin sections are established.
    [MED-EPI-p0067-s05] This leads to local nucleosomal condensation at regulatory sites and, in consequence, reduced DNA accessibility for TFs.
- MED-EPI-C02-S3-01 | S3
  ATOM: In contrast to Drosophila, where the role of the H2Aub mark is not well understood, in mammals H2Aub facilitates recruitment of PRC2 via JARID2.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0067-s20] In contrast to Drosophila, where the role of H2Aub is not well understood, in mammals this mark facilitates recruitment of PRC2 via JARID2.
- MED-EPI-C02-S3-02 | S3
  ATOM: Cytosine methylation of CpG islands prevents recruitment of PcG complexes, which suggests an antagonism between DNA methylation and PcG proteins, at least in CG-rich DNA.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0034-s07] CG-rich DNA appears to be recognized by the PcG complexes that establish
    [MED-EPI-p0034-s08] H3K27me3 and H2AK119ub. Cytosine methylation of CpG islands prevents recruitment, suggesting an antagonism between DNA methylation and PcG proteins, at least in CG-rich DNA.
- MED-EPI-C02-S3-03 | S3
  ATOM: Although Hox gene regulation supports a view of PcG function as stable and heritable repression, most of the other identified PcG target genes change expression over time or across the cell cycle, or are subjected to short-term environmental control.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0068-s08] Indeed, the regulation of Hox genes, defining long-lasting cellular identities, nicely supports this restricted view of PcG function.
    [MED-EPI-p0068-s09] However, most of the other PcG target genes identified change expression over time, the cell cycle or are even subjected to short-term environmental control.
